questions.question: How do methods and return work in Ruby?
questions.title: Methods and Return in Ruby
questions.direct_answer: A method is defined with def: def greet(name); "Hello, #{name}"; end. Ruby returns the last expression by default (implicit return) — no need for `return` unless you exit early. def add(a,b); a + b; end returns a+b. Arguments: required (a), default (a=1), keyword (name:), splat (*args collects extras into an array), double-splat (**opts collects keyword args into a hash). Methods are called with or without parens (puts 'hi' or puts('hi')). `return` exits immediately (return x if x.nil?); without a value, returns nil. Methods end with end. Method naming: snake_case; predicate methods end with ? (empty?); dangerous ones with ! (save!). Every call returns something (nil if nothing else).

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know def/end, implicit return (last expression), default/keyword/splat args, and ?/! naming.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Adding explicit `return` everywhere (Ruby returns the last expression), or using parens inconsistently.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Methods: def name(args); ...; end. Implicit return (last expression). Args: required, default (a=1), keyword (name:), *args, **opts. snake_case; ? predicates, ! dangerous.

sections.title: Method Anatomy
sections.content:
def name(args)...end. Implicit return. Args: required/default/keyword/*args/**opts. snake_case; ?/! naming.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  D[def greet(name)] --> B[body: last expr = return]
  B --> R[implicit return]
  A[args] --> Re[required a]
  A --> De[default a=1]
  A --> K[keyword name:]
  A --> S[splat *args / **opts]
```

sections.title: Methods and return
sections.content:
```ruby
# Define a method
def greet(name)
  "Hello, #{name}"     # last expression -> IMPLICIT return
end
greet('Ada')            # 'Hello, Ada'

# Implicit return: no `return` needed (last expression is returned)
def add(a, b)
  a + b                  # returns a + b
end

# `return` exits EARLY:
def find_first(xs)
  xs.each { |x| return x if x > 0 }   # exit early
  nil                    # default
end

# Arguments:
def f(a, b = 1, name:, *args, **opts)
  # a: required; b: default (1); name: keyword (required);
  # *args: extras -> Array; **opts: keyword extras -> Hash
end
f(10, name: 'Ada', 1, 2, extra: 'x')

# Call with or without parens (both fine):
puts 'hi'
puts('hi')

# Naming: snake_case; ? = predicate (returns bool); ! = dangerous
arr.empty?    # ? -> returns true/false
arr.sort!     # ! -> mutates in place (dangerous)

# Every call returns something (nil if nothing else):
result = [1,2].each { |x| x }   # returns [1,2] (each returns the original)
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Adding explicit `return` everywhere — Ruby returns the last expression.
Using parens inconsistently (pick a style; Ruby allows both).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: A method is def name(args) ... end; Ruby returns the last expression (implicit return).
`return` exits early; without a value, returns nil.
Args: required (a), default (a=1), keyword (name:), splat (*args), double-splat (**opts).
Call with or without parens (puts 'hi' or puts('hi')).
